title: A larger planet of equal mass
hook: Change planet radius and predict surface gravitational acceleration.
misconception: surface gravitational acceleration doubles when planet radius doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply g = GM/R² to compare surface gravitational acceleration when planet radius changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a spherically symmetric planet with fixed mass, g = GM/R². When planet radius doubles, surface gravitational acceleration becomes ¼ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model g = GM/R²; scaling exponent -2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a spherically symmetric planet with fixed mass, with a nonzero initial result. If planet radius triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on surface gravitational acceleration?
recall.why: Apply g = GM/R² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/9.
